sources.what: 25 world-map snapshots, 2000 BCE → 2010 CE, sampled from a single worldwide polity dataset and merged into one file the year slider filters live.
sources.note: Coarse, scholarly-approximate polygons for roughly 1,600 polities spanning 3400 BCE-2024 CE - not an authoritative or legally recognized boundary claim. Coverage is deliberately curated to notable/major polities rather than exhaustive, so earlier eras show fewer, larger territories than a maximal atlas would.

sources.what: 347 notable battles with a named war/conflict, curated by Wikipedia-language-edition coverage, capped per century.
sources.note: A curated sample, not a complete record — only battles tagged with coordinates, a date, and a named conflict are included, and each century keeps only its most-covered entries.

sources.what: 8x8km elevation clip (contours, elevation bands, hand-authored river line) around Canne della Battaglia, Apulia — the Cannae battlefield.
sources.source: Terrarium DEM tiles (s3://elevation-tiles-prod, Mapzen/Tilezen "joerd"); underlying source over this area is EU-DEM (Copernicus Land Monitoring Service)
sources.license: Copernicus free-and-open-data policy — required attribution: "Produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union - EU-DEM layers."
sources.note: The river line is a hand-authored trace of the DEM's own valley (today's course), not a record of the disputed 216 BC channel.

sources.what: 16 units and 7 phases choreographing the double envelopment, with terrain-aware routed movement between authored anchor points.
sources.source: Authored from general knowledge of Polybius (Histories, Book III) and Livy (Ab Urbe Condita, Book XXII), both public-domain ancient sources
sources.license: Public domain (ancient sources); choreography, positions and routing are this app's own reconstruction
sources.note: A simplified reconstruction, not a record — unit counts, formation depths and exact geometry are approximate; the ancient sources themselves disagree on troop totals.
